rows.description: An adult names what happened, apologises without excuses, asks what would help, and changes the behaviour; undoing through ritual is replaced by repair that the other person can feel.

rows.description: A child says yes cheerfully to a chore and then conveniently forgets every time; unable to say no directly, the resistance comes out sideways.

rows.description: A teenager who resents a rule complies with a scowl, moves at a snail's pace and answers in monosyllables; the anger is real but disguised as compliance.

rows.description: A student finds sarcastic notes of thanks for washing dishes for once and feels attacked without a fair chance to reply; asking calmly what the roommate wants to change is a way out.
